learningObjectives: Use Pulse to post, view, and reply to messages with case stakeholders and teams
Explain how developers and users each access Pulse
Configure Tags to classify Pulse messages and find related Cases
Recognize Pulse email notification triggers and reply-by-email behavior

elements.description: Pega's built-in messaging system. Users post, view, and reply in the Pulse Activity Feed — directed to specific users, team members, or Case stakeholders. Example: a CSR posts once to update every Case participant on a claim's status.

elements.text: Think of a discussion board beside the work: authorized colleagues can exchange context without relying on someone forwarding a separate email thread. Visibility and retention still depend on the application configuration.

elements.description: Pulse collaboration access differs by role:
items: DEVELOPERS — click 'Toggle developer collaboration' in the App Studio header
USERS — access Pulse via a Pulse widget on their Case or Work Object

elements.description: Reply to a Pulse message with or without a comment. Users opt into email notifications for @-mentions, likes, replies in conversations they participated in, or posts to Cases they follow. Email replies appear as Pulse comments without login.

elements.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 760 180" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img"><title>Collaboration and categorization</title><desc>Pulse discussions, Tags for related information, and optional email notification responses.</desc><rect x="10" y="15" width="740" height="150" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface-1)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><g fill="var(--pa-ink)" font-family="system-ui" font-size="17"><text x="30" y="50">Pulse: discussion in the relevant application or Case context</text><text x="30" y="88">Tags: categorize messages and discover related work</text><text x="30" y="126">Optional email notifications: reply returns to the conversation</text></g></svg>
elements.caption: Pulse discussion, tag-based discovery and configured email notifications have distinct purposes. Neither mentioning nor tagging establishes access permissions.

elements.description: Descriptive words or phrases ASSOCIATED WITH A PULSE MESSAGE that categorize messages so users can quickly find information to resolve a Case. Add a tag by typing # followed by a word/phrase WITHOUT SPACES.
Lists tags relevant to a Case. Each tag is a link — clicking it shows all Cases sharing that tag. Added to the Full Case Page (not the Navigation bar, where the Pulse widget lives).

elements.title: Collaboration Tool Matcher

examPitfalls.title: Two ways to access Pulse
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Developers use the Toggle developer collaboration pane in App Studio; users use a Pulse widget on the portal Navigation bar.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Match the access path to the audience; the user Pulse widget must be configured by a developer.

examPitfalls.title: Pulse email notification triggers
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Users choose email notifications for the listed events. A reference is not the only listed event, and a notification preference must not be omitted from the scenario.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Know the four triggers; users can reply from the email without logging in.

examPitfalls.title: Reply with or without a comment
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The topic permits a response with or without a written comment. Do not infer a particular emoji feature from that statement alone.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Distinguish acknowledgment, written response and direct email comment.

examPitfalls.title: Tags use # and no spaces
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A tag is entered with the # symbol followed by a word/phrase with NO spaces; tags attach to Pulse messages.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Create a tag with #word or reuse a recent one.

examPitfalls.title: Tags widget is a clickable link
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what happens when a user clicks a tag in the Tags widget. Candidates say 'nothing; tags are display-only.' Clicking a tag in the Tags widget opens a filtered view of all cases with that tag — tags are interactive navigation links.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the Tags widget on the full case page to navigate related Cases.

examPitfalls.title: Widget placement
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The topic describes portal navigation and Case work-area integration; it does not provide a universal editor path for every UI architecture.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the supported integration for the target portal and version.

examPitfalls.title: Cross-module connections
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions describe a user needing to see collaboration updates across multiple modules. Candidates say Pulse is per-Case only. Pulse notifications and tags can surface in any portal that includes the relevant widget — cross-module visibility depends on portal configuration.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pulse may involve optional email notifications; Send email workflow automation has a different trigger. Classification is not a permission mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A CSR must update every participant on an automobile claim about its payment status in one place inside the Case. Which tool fits?

options.text: Pulse — post a single message in the Case's activity feed to the participants
A Send email Step to each participant individually
A Tag on the Case
An Access Role update

practiceQuiz.hint: In-Case messaging posted to Case stakeholders and participants is called Pulse.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pulse expresses the requested discussion in the work context.

optionExplanations.A: Pulse expresses the requested discussion in the work context.
optionExplanations.B: Separate automated emails do not supply the requested single discussion feed.
optionExplanations.C: A classification label is not the requested status message.
optionExplanations.D: Changing a role does not post the requested discussion update.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer wants to open the developer collaboration pane in App Studio. Which documented access path fits?

options.text: Click 'Toggle developer collaboration' in the App Studio header to open the Developer collaboration pane
Add a Pulse widget to the Navigation bar
Open Admin Studio's collaboration console
Enable a Data Page that streams messages

practiceQuiz.hint: Developers use the collaboration pane in App Studio.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The header control opens the documented developer collaboration pane.

optionExplanations.A: The header control opens the documented developer collaboration pane.
optionExplanations.B: A portal widget addresses user access rather than this developer-pane request.
optionExplanations.C: The cited access path is not an administration console.
optionExplanations.D: A data-page streaming design is not the documented pane control.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is explaining Pega's collaboration features to a project team and is asked how an end user gets access to Pulse in their portal. How does an end user get Pulse added to their portal?

options.text: A developer adds a Pulse widget to the portal Navigation bar (or embeds it in a Case's work area)
Users automatically see Pulse everywhere with no configuration
Users open the Developer collaboration pane
Users install a browser extension

practiceQuiz.hint: User access = Pulse widget on the Navigation bar.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A developer configures the supported user-facing widget or integration.

optionExplanations.A: A developer configures the supported user-facing widget or integration.
optionExplanations.B: The cited user access requires the relevant portal configuration.
optionExplanations.C: The developer pane is a different access context.
optionExplanations.D: A browser extension is not the documented portal integration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user has chosen to receive Pulse email notifications. Which TWO documented events can trigger them?

options.text: Someone @-mentions the user or one of their teams
Someone posts a Pulse message to a Case the user follows
The user's password is about to expire
A Ruleset is locked

practiceQuiz.hint: Which two specific Pulse interaction types trigger an email notification to a user?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A reference to the user or team is a listed event after opting in. A message on a followed Case is another listed notification event.

optionExplanations.A: A reference to the user or team is a listed event after opting in.
optionExplanations.B: A message on a followed Case is another listed notification event.
optionExplanations.C: Password expiry is not a Pulse conversation event in this list.
optionExplanations.D: Locking a ruleset is not a Pulse conversation event in this list.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user receives a Pulse email notification. Can they respond without logging into Pega?

options.text: Yes — they can reply from the email, and the reply appears as a comment on the top message
No — they must log in to the portal to reply
Only if they are an application developer
Only by phone to the administrator

practiceQuiz.hint: Determine whether Pulse email notifications allow a direct reply without logging into Pega.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The described email response returns as a comment to the conversation.

optionExplanations.A: The described email response returns as a comment to the conversation.
optionExplanations.B: The source explicitly describes responding without logging in.
optionExplanations.C: The described response capability is not restricted to developers.
optionExplanations.D: A telephone call is not the described message reply mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is training new team members on Pega's collaboration tools and explains how to tag Pulse messages for searchability. How do you add the tag 'innovation' to a Pulse message?

options.text: Type # followed by the word with no spaces (e.g., #innovation), or pick a recently used tag
Type @ followed by the word
Wrap the word in quotes
Add it as an Access Role

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the exact syntax for adding a tag to a Pulse message — which character and spacing rule applies?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The hashtag syntax or recent-tag selection identifies the label.

optionExplanations.A: The hashtag syntax or recent-tag selection identifies the label.
optionExplanations.B: The at sign references a user or team rather than adding this tag.
optionExplanations.C: Quotation marks do not establish the documented tagging syntax.
optionExplanations.D: An access role is not a message classification label.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the Tags widget, what happens when a user clicks a tag?

options.text: A dialog opens listing the Cases tagged with that word or phrase — the tag acts as a link
The tag is deleted from the Case
A new Case is created with that tag
The application restarts to apply the tag

practiceQuiz.hint: A tag is a clickable link to tagged Cases.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The widget’s tag link opens the documented related-Case dialog.

optionExplanations.A: The widget’s tag link opens the documented related-Case dialog.
optionExplanations.B: Selecting this link does not express a delete operation.
optionExplanations.C: Selecting an existing label does not express Case creation.
optionExplanations.D: The described navigation does not require an application restart.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where does a developer add the Pulse widget versus the Tags widget?

options.text: Pulse widget → the portal Navigation bar; Tags widget → the full case page
Both widgets go only on the Navigation bar
Both widgets go only on the full case page
Neither can be added in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Pulse = nav bar; Tags = full case page.
practiceQuiz.rationale: These are the placements described by the cited introductory procedure.

optionExplanations.A: These are the placements described by the cited introductory procedure.
optionExplanations.B: The Tags widget placement is not limited to the navigation bar.
optionExplanations.C: The source also describes portal navigation for Pulse.
optionExplanations.D: The source describes configuring these widgets from App Studio.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A CSR wants to ask a legal colleague a question without leaving the case UI or sending external email. Which Pega feature is designed for this?

options.text: Pulse — in-case messaging where team members can post messages, @mention colleagues, and attach files
Send Email shape — triggers automated email to the legal team from within the case process
Co-Browse — shares the CSR screen with the legal colleague for simultaneous viewing
Case Locking — assigns exclusive edit access to the legal colleague so they can add input

practiceQuiz.hint: Which tool enables inline case communication without external tools?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Contextual discussion fits the requested collaboration task.

optionExplanations.A: Contextual discussion fits the requested collaboration task.
optionExplanations.B: Automated correspondence does not directly express this inline conversation.
optionExplanations.C: Screen sharing is different from the requested written discussion.
optionExplanations.D: Locking work addresses concurrency rather than message exchange.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Jane has chosen Pulse email notifications. A colleague references her with @JaneSmith. Which statement matches the documented notification behavior?

options.text: This is one of the events for which Jane can receive a Pulse email notification
References can never generate Pulse email notifications
The reference automatically grants new Case edit permissions
The reference necessarily creates a blocking Assignment

practiceQuiz.hint: Consider the user’s notification preference; a mention is not an access grant.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The chosen notification preference includes this reference event.

optionExplanations.A: The chosen notification preference includes this reference event.
optionExplanations.B: The topic expressly lists references among email events.
optionExplanations.C: A mention does not by itself configure new access permissions.
optionExplanations.D: Mentioning someone is not itself a formal blocking workflow task.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documented portal model, can users incorporate Pulse messaging in the main work area of a Case?

options.text: Yes, using the supported Pulse integration for the portal
No, the source restricts it to a developer-only pane
Only by treating a Tag as a message feed
A user’s password setting defines the placement

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish the user portal from the developer collaboration pane.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The cited portal description permits this work-area integration.

optionExplanations.A: The cited portal description permits this work-area integration.
optionExplanations.B: The source distinguishes user portal integration from the developer pane.
optionExplanations.C: Tags and a conversation feed have different purposes.
optionExplanations.D: Authentication preferences do not determine widget placement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user wants to locate related Cases by selecting an existing label in the Tags widget. What documented behavior supports this?

options.text: The tag opens a dialog listing Cases tagged with that word or phrase
The tag automatically creates a replacement Case
The tag grants access to every Case regardless of permissions
The tag guarantees all Pulse messages are permanent Insights records

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the documented Tags widget interaction; do not infer storage or query architecture.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This is the widget navigation behavior described in the topic.

optionExplanations.A: This is the widget navigation behavior described in the topic.
optionExplanations.B: The link discovers tagged work rather than creating a new Case.
optionExplanations.C: Classification does not establish unrestricted access rights.
optionExplanations.D: The source does not establish this permanent storage or Insights guarantee.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining the purpose of Tags in Pega Pulse. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Tags function?

options.text: Tags categorize or relate Pulse messages by topic
A tag in the Tags widget links to a dialog of Cases with that tag
Adding a Tag to a Pulse message automatically creates a new Case linked to that tag
Pulse Tags replace Case Status as the primary mechanism for tracking Case progress in Pega

practiceQuiz.hint: Tags are for classification and discoverability of Pulse messages — they do not create Cases or replace status.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A label relates messages about a common topic. The widget supports finding Cases with the selected label.

optionExplanations.A: A label relates messages about a common topic.
optionExplanations.B: The widget supports finding Cases with the selected label.
optionExplanations.C: Classification does not itself create another Case.
optionExplanations.D: Labels do not replace the workflow progress model.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With Pulse email notifications configured and chosen by the user, which TWO behaviors are described in the collaboration topic?

options.text: Messages on a followed Case are one of the listed notification events
A direct email response is displayed as a comment on the conversation’s top message
Pulse email notifications are broadcast to all Pega operators in the application regardless of their participation in the Case
Pulse email notifications require a separate correspondence Ruleset to be imported from Pega Marketplace

practiceQuiz.hint: Pulse notifications go to Case participants — not all users — and reply-by-email posts back to the Case.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Followed work is one of the configured notification events. The response is a comment in the related conversation.

optionExplanations.A: Followed work is one of the configured notification events.
optionExplanations.B: The response is a comment in the related conversation.
optionExplanations.C: The described preferences and events are not a universal operator broadcast.
optionExplanations.D: The cited procedure does not require the invented Marketplace import.

quickRecap.value: OOTB messaging: post/view/reply in the activity feed to users, teams, or Case/app stakeholders.
Developers: Toggle developer collaboration pane (App Studio). Users: Pulse widget on the Navigation bar.
Reply with/without a comment. Email triggers: @-mention · like · comment in participated convo · post to a followed Case. Reply from email without logging in.
Words/phrases on a Pulse message to classify/relate; add with # + word, NO spaces; create new or reuse recent.
Lists a Case's tags; each tag is a LINK to a dialog of tagged Cases; added to the full case page.
